Compute the log-likelihood of a transition tree

Source: R/likelihood.R
logLik.transitiontrees.Rd

logLik() computes the log-likelihood of a fitted tree: the sum, over every observed position, of the log probability that the tree assigned to the state that occurred, given the longest context of the tree that matches the preceding history. It is the basis of the information criteria and of perplexity, and allows trees with different depths, pruning or smoothing to be compared on the same data.

Without newdata, the log-likelihood is computed in-sample from the fitted counts. With newdata, the sequences are scored under the fitted tree, which gives the held-out log-likelihood. A state that is not among the tree's states is not scored, and the position after it is predicted from the root; the reported number of observations counts only scored positions. The number of parameters is the number of contexts times \(k - 1\), for \(k\) states.

The result is a logLik object and works with AIC() and BIC(). model_fit() returns log-likelihood, AIC, BIC and perplexity together as a table.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'transitiontrees'
logLik(object, newdata = NULL, ...)

Arguments

object

A transitiontrees object.

newdata

Sequences to score, in any form accepted by context_tree(). NULL (default) gives the in-sample log-likelihood.

...

Not used.

Value

An object of class logLik: the log-likelihood (natural logarithm), with attributes df (number of parameters) and nobs (number of scored positions).

Conditions

transitiontrees_bad_input when newdata has an unsupported type or no usable sequence.

See also

model_fit(), perplexity(), score_sequences(), nobs.transitiontrees().

Examples

tree <- context_tree(trajectories, max_depth = 2)
logLik(tree)
#> 'log Lik.' -1565.772 (df=26)
AIC(tree)
#> [1] 3183.543
logLik(tree, newdata = engagement)
#> 'log Lik.' -18657.84 (df=26)
